claims.text: The A2A protocol is an open standard for communication between AI agents, enabling agents built with different frameworks, vendors, or organizations to work together.
A2A complements MCP: A2A standardizes communication among agents across organizations and frameworks, while MCP connects models to data and external resources.
MCP tools are typically stateless and perform specific, predefined functions such as a calculator or a database query.
A2A supports complex, multi-turn interactions in which agents reason, plan, delegate tasks, negotiate, or ask for clarification, rather than interacting like tools.
A2A crosses the boundary between agents, whereas MCP stays within one agent, connecting it to APIs and enterprise applications.
In the A2A flow, a client fetches the server's Agent Card (e.g., at /.well-known/agent-card.json) to learn its capabilities and endpoint.
In A2A authentication, the client reads the Agent Card's security schemes and, for an openIdConnect scheme, obtains a JWT token via the authorizationUrl and tokenUrl.
A2A clients send messages with either SendMessage (single request/response) or SendStreamingMessage (a stream of task updates).
A2A natively supports long-running operations, handling streaming with Server-Sent Events (SSE) and asynchronous execution.
OpenAI's Responses API supports remote MCP servers via the 'mcp' tool type, over either Streamable HTTP or HTTP/SSE transports.
OpenAI warns that some MCP servers expose dozens of tools, and exposing many tools to the model can result in high cost and latency; the allowed_tools parameter imports only a subset.

By default, OpenAI requests approval before any data is shared with a remote MCP server or connector; this creates an mcp_approval_request output item, and each approval applies to a single tool call.
The require_approval parameter can be set to 'never' to skip approvals for all tools on a server, or to an object listing only the tools that skip approval.
OpenAI warns that a malicious remote MCP server can exfiltrate sensitive data from anything that enters the model's context, and advises using only trusted servers.

OpenAI recommends using require_approval and allowed_tools to ensure sensitive actions always go through an approval flow, and recommends reviewing or logging all data shared with a remote MCP server.
For OpenAI's MCP tool, OAuth access tokens are passed in the authorization field, and OAuth client registration and authorization must be handled separately by the application.
OpenAI's Secure MCP Tunnel (tunnel_id) connects private, on-premises, or firewalled MCP servers to supported OpenAI products without exposing them to the public internet.
OpenAI's built-in connectors (e.g., Gmail, Google Drive, SharePoint) carry a risk of sending sensitive data to OpenAI or giving models read access to sensitive data in those services.

In Microsoft Copilot Studio, each MCP server is added to an agent as a tool; all of its tools are on by default and an administrator can turn off 'Allow all' to disable individual tools, after which new server tools are off by default.
In Copilot Studio, MCP access relies on Power Platform connectors, so a data policy regulating those connectors also regulates access to the MCP server and its tools.
Microsoft Foundry Agent Service accepts only remote MCP server endpoints; local MCP servers must be self-hosted, e.g., on Azure Container Apps or Azure Functions.

Foundry Toolbox gives agents a single MCP-compatible endpoint so tools can be added, removed, or reconfigured without changing agent code, and it works with runtimes such as Microsoft Agent Framework and LangGraph.

Foundry supports MCP auth types including no auth, custom-keys headers (e.g., GitHub PAT), OAuth (Foundry-managed or bring-your-own app), user Entra token, project managed identity, and agentic identity.
Foundry non-streaming MCP tool calls time out after 100 seconds; longer operations require background mode with a supported model, and long-running MCP tasks support is in preview.
Foundry private MCP server connectivity requires Standard Agent Setup with private networking (BYO VNet); basic agent setup does not support private MCP endpoints.
